title: An instance can be Active with large rate limits while its risk-framework coverage is still marked Pending
content:
Each Instance Configuration Document opens with an `RRC Framework Full Implementation` flag. Aave Core USDC (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.2.2.1), Aave Core USDS (.2.3.1), Aave Core USDT (.2.4.1), Aave USDe (.2.5.1), Maple USDC (.3.1.1) and Maple USDT (.3.2.1) all read "**`Covered`**".

The Ethena USDe instance (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.4.1.1) reads "**`Pending`**" — and it is filed inside a container that stores "the Ethereum Mainnet Instances of the Ethena Protocol with `Active` Status" (.4). Its limits are not nominal either: inflow `maxAmount` 250,000,000 USDC with a 100,000,000 per day slope, and outflow `maxAmount` 500,000,000 USDe (.4.1.2.4.1/.2).

So the Artifact permits a live, largest-in-class conduit whose framework coverage is by its own declaration incomplete. The flag is being used as a disclosure rather than as a gate: it tells a reader where the review debt sits instead of preventing the exposure from existing.

That is a defensible engineering choice — operational reality outruns documentation, and naming the gap is better than hiding it — but it is a real tension. The same instance also defers its Underlying Asset Address (.4.1.2.2.2) and its `delegatedSigner` addresses (.4.1.3.1.1) to a future iteration. The venue with the weakest documentation in the chunk is also among the largest by permitted flow, which inverts the usual expectation that scrutiny scales with size.
description: Every other instance in this chunk declares RRC Framework Full Implementation as Covered; Ethena USDe declares Pending yet carries a 250,000,000 USDC inflow ceiling and 100,000,000 per day slope.
